nodes.name: Mode 1: Script to Video
nodes.summary: User provides a script or brief; LLM reads text and infers intent from language, structure, and stated goals.

details.definition: The Unified Intelligence reads the script text, the brand context (from Graphiti if available), and the project brief. It outputs genre_parameters and moment_weights directly from understanding the written content.
details.rationale: This is the simpler case — the LLM reads text and infers intent from language, structure, and stated goals.
details.modulates: Outputs CreativeIntent (genre_parameters + moment_weights + narrative_strategy)

nodes.name: Mode 2: Raw Footage to Edited Video
nodes.summary: User uploads footage with no script; computation must happen in stages (clean before measuring) to avoid garbage from filler/false-starts/warm-up.

details.definition: Raw footage is a mess: repeated takes, fillers, false starts, warm-up energy, no music, no structure. Computing genre_parameters from raw footage directly would produce garbage — the measurements include all the bad parts that will be cut. The computation must happen in STAGES, cleaning before measuring.
details.rationale: When no script exists, the clean transcript BECOMES the retroactive script. The system doesn't need a user-written script — it needs to understand what the content says and how it should feel. The transcript provides that.
details.modulates: Outputs CreativeIntent via 5-stage pipeline

nodes.name: Stage 1 — Transcribe and Clean
nodes.summary: Whisper transcription, filler detection, false-start detection, best-take selection (fuzzy Jaccard) producing clean transcript + segment map.

details.definition: Input: Raw video file(s). Action: Whisper transcription → filler detection → false start detection → best-take selection (fuzzy Jaccard). Output: Clean transcript (only the good parts) + segment map (which timestamps to keep).
details.rationale: This pipeline already exists in raw-footage-processor.ts
examples: raw-footage-processor.ts

nodes.name: Stage 2 — Analyze CONTENT from Clean Transcript
nodes.summary: NLP analysis on clean transcript text to identify topics, claims, questions, and CTA presence — independent of audio delivery quality.

details.definition: Input: Clean transcript text. Action: NLP analysis — entity extraction, topic structure, vocabulary analysis, sentence classification. Output: What the content is ABOUT: topics discussed, claims made, questions asked, CTA presence.
details.rationale: Text analysis only. Independent of audio delivery quality

nodes.name: Stage 3 — Analyze VISUAL SETUP from Footage
nodes.summary: Scene classification, face detection, shot scale, lighting analysis on raw video keyframes — observations stable across edits.

details.definition: Input: Raw video keyframes. Action: Scene classification, face detection, shot scale analysis, lighting analysis. Output: Visual context — indoor/outdoor, single/multi person, shot types available, production quality.
details.rationale: These observations don't change after editing — studio shot stays studio shot

nodes.name: Stage 4 — Compute Speech Signals on BEST TAKES ONLY
nodes.summary: Speech energy, speaking rate, pitch analysis on best-take segments only (the dish, not the raw ingredients).

details.definition: Input: Audio from best-take segments (not the full raw audio). Action: Speech energy, speaking rate, pitch analysis — but ONLY on the segments that will be used. Output: Accurate speech characteristics of the final content.
details.rationale: Critical difference from naive approach — measuring the dish, not the raw ingredients

nodes.name: Stage 5 — Unified Intelligence Sets the Dials
nodes.summary: Single Gemini call reads cleaned content + visual setup + speech signals + brand context and outputs CreativeIntent object.

details.definition: Input: Clean transcript content (Stage 2) + visual setup (Stage 3) + speech signals from best takes (Stage 4) + brand context from Graphiti. Action: Single Gemini call reads all inputs and outputs the CreativeIntent object. Output: genre_parameters + moment_weights + narrative_strategy.
details.rationale: The LLM is computing dials from cleaned, selected, representative data — not from raw mess

nodes.name: Brand Context from Graphiti (Both Modes)
nodes.summary: If brand has been edited before (project #10+), Graphiti provides learned preferences that OVERRIDE computed defaults.

details.definition: If this brand has been edited before (project #10+), Graphiti provides learned preferences: which genre_parameter values the user kept vs overrode for this brand, which techniques the user consistently rejects, visual style preferences (warm/cool, high/low graphics density). These learned preferences OVERRIDE the computed defaults.
details.rationale: By project #50, the system has essentially memorized how this brand should be edited.

nodes.name: pacing_tolerance
nodes.summary: Seconds before a hold becomes 'too long'. Sets the threshold for when to consider cutting.

details.modulates: time_since_last_cut threshold and all pacing-related signal triggers
examples: Product launch: pacing_tolerance = 3, time_since_last_cut > 3.0 → consider cutting
Luxury brand film: pacing_tolerance = 8, time_since_last_cut > 8.0 → consider cutting
UGC/social: pacing_tolerance = 2, time_since_last_cut > 2.0 → consider cutting
details.rationale: The same doc handles every content type without content-type-specific sections. Content type is EMERGENT from genre_parameters.

nodes.name: energy_baseline
nodes.summary: What 'normal' energy means for this project. Anything above is 'energetic', below is 'reflective'.

details.modulates: Energy thresholds — system treats anything above as 'energetic' and below as 'reflective'
details.rationale: Literally the average of observed energy in the good takes. If speech_energy averages 0.5 across best takes, baseline IS 0.5.

nodes.name: transition_density
nodes.summary: Target transitions per minute.

details.modulates: Transition placement and frequency
details.rationale: Roughly: 60 / pacing_tolerance = transitions per minute baseline. Music-driven content (low speech, high music): transitions sync to beats, density from BPM. Speech-driven content: transitions at topic boundaries and energy shifts.

nodes.name: graphic_density
nodes.summary: Target graphics per minute (stat graphics, callouts, lower thirds).

details.modulates: Graphic placement and frequency
details.rationale: If the speaker mentions 8 numbers in 2 minutes → up to 4 graphics/min is justified. High formality → fewer, more restrained graphics. Low formality → more, punchier graphics (social style).

nodes.name: silence_tolerance
nodes.summary: Seconds before silence is treated as error / dead air.

details.modulates: Silence removal triggers
details.rationale: Formal + slow speaker → tolerance up to 2-3 seconds (pauses are deliberate). Casual + fast speaker → tolerance 0.3-0.5 seconds (pauses are dead air).

nodes.name: zoom_budget
nodes.summary: Max zoom moves per video.

details.modulates: Zoom decision frequency
details.rationale: More emphasis moments → more zoom opportunities. But capped: roughly 1 zoom per 15-30 seconds max, diminishing returns after that.

nodes.name: caption_style
nodes.summary: Caption rendering style — word-by-word, phrase, subtitle, or karaoke.

details.modulates: Caption renderer behavior and timing granularity

nodes.name: color_temperature
nodes.summary: Color grade temperature target.

details.modulates: Color grade pipeline target

nodes.name: formality
nodes.summary: 0=raw/UGC, 1=broadcast/cinematic. Influences pace, silence tolerance, graphic restraint.

details.modulates: pacing_tolerance, silence_tolerance, graphic_density restraint
details.rationale: Studio + formal speech + high production value → formality 0.7-0.9. Handheld + casual speech + raw look → formality 0.1-0.3.

nodes.name: moment_weight_map Schema
nodes.summary: Per-segment narrative importance map. Each entry has segment_id and weight (0-1). 0.8+ amplifies, 0.3- suppresses, 0.5 default.

details.definition: moment_weights: [ { segment_id: string, weight: float } ] // 0-1, where 0.8+ = amplify, 0.3- = suppress
details.modulates: Technique intensity. Each Part 2 mapping includes a weight_response field showing how moment_weight scales the technique.
examples: weight 0.9 + zoom_push → zoom_punch (amplified)
weight 0.3 + zoom_push → skip or gentle drift (suppressed)
weight 0.5 = default, no modification
weight 0.9: stat_graphic (large, animated counter, with zoom_push and SFX)
weight 0.5: stat_graphic (standard size, fade-in, no complement)
weight 0.2: caption_emphasis only (highlight number in accent color, no separate graphic)
details.rationale: The moment_weight_map is a per-segment intensity multiplier. Each Part 2 mapping includes a weight_response field showing how moment_weight scales the technique.

nodes.name: narrative_strategy Schema (optional)
nodes.summary: Optional structural metadata for complex content — structure, cross-cut detection, emotional arc, loop structure.

details.definition: narrative_strategy: { structure: string (three-act | hook-value-cta | kishōtenketsu | etc.), cross_cut: boolean (parallel storylines detected?), cross_cut_segments: array (which segments intercut, if applicable), emotional_arc: string (building | declining | wave | sustained | shock), loop_structure: boolean (end connects to beginning? for social replay) }
details.rationale: Optional, for complex content

nodes.name: has_speaker
nodes.summary: Boolean — does the content feature a speaker?

details.modulates: Whether speech-driven techniques (subtitles, audio ducking, transcript-driven graphics) apply

nodes.name: has_multiple_speakers
nodes.summary: Boolean — multiple speakers detected (interview, panel, dialogue).

details.modulates: Speaker labeling, lower-third placement, dialogue cutting strategy

nodes.name: has_narration
nodes.summary: Boolean — voiceover narration present.

details.modulates: VO ducking, music bed levels, subtitle policy

nodes.name: has_music_primary
nodes.summary: Boolean — music IS the content (music video, montage).

details.definition: has_music_primary: boolean — music IS the content (music video, montage)
details.modulates: Beat-sync vs speech-sync transitions; whether transitions use BPM-driven density

nodes.name: has_product
nodes.summary: Boolean — product visible / featured in content.

details.modulates: Product callouts, hero shot weighting, brand placement strategies

nodes.name: has_demonstration
nodes.summary: Boolean — demonstration/how-to content detected.

details.modulates: Step graphics, slow-pacing on demo segments, before/after framing

nodes.name: has_testimonial
nodes.summary: Boolean — customer testimonial detected.

details.modulates: Lower-thirds with name/role, quote graphics, B-roll under VO strategy

nodes.name: target_platform
nodes.summary: Target delivery platform — affects aspect ratio, length, captioning style, LUFS target.

details.range: enum: youtube | reels | tiktok | linkedin | etc.
details.modulates: Aspect ratio, length, caption style defaults, LUFS normalization target

nodes.name: target_culture
nodes.summary: Target audience culture — affects color grade defaults, density expectations.

details.range: enum: western-default | east-asian | indian | middle-eastern | etc.
details.modulates: Color grade defaults, density expectations, narrative pacing conventions

nodes.name: Signal Thresholds Are Relative to Genre Parameters
nodes.summary: Every signal threshold in Part 2 is RELATIVE to genre_parameters, not absolute. Same doc handles every content type without content-type-specific sections.

details.definition: Every signal threshold in Part 2 is RELATIVE to genre_parameters, not absolute. The mapping in Part 2 says: time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance → consider_cut. The genre_parameters say what pacing_tolerance IS for this project.
details.rationale: This means the same doc handles every content type without content-type-specific sections. Content type is EMERGENT from genre_parameters.
examples: time_since_last_cut > pacing_tolerance → consider_cut

nodes.name: Moment Weights Modulate Technique Intensity
nodes.summary: Moment weight is a per-segment intensity multiplier; each Part 2 mapping has a weight_response field showing how it scales the technique.

details.definition: The moment_weight_map is a per-segment intensity multiplier. Each Part 2 mapping includes a weight_response field showing how moment_weight scales the technique.
examples: weight 0.9: stat_graphic (large, animated counter, with zoom_push and SFX)
weight 0.5: stat_graphic (standard size, fade-in, no complement)
weight 0.2: caption_emphasis only (highlight number in accent color, no separate graphic)

nodes.name: Section-level Weights (10+ minute content)
nodes.summary: For long content. Content divided into 5-8 major sections; each section gets a weight. Scenes inherit unless overridden.

details.definition: Long content (10+ minutes): Section-level weights. The content is divided into 5-8 major sections. Each section gets a weight. Scenes within sections inherit the section weight unless explicitly overridden.
examples: { level: 'section', id: 'product-demo', weight: 0.9 }
{ level: 'section', id: 'intro-context', weight: 0.4 }

nodes.name: Scene-level Weights (3-10 minute content)
nodes.summary: For medium content. Each scene (5-15 scenes) gets a weight; signal system handles moment-by-moment within scene.

details.definition: Medium content (3-10 minutes): Scene-level weights. Each scene (typically 5-15 scenes) gets a weight. Within each scene, the signal system handles moment-by-moment decisions autonomously. The weight tells it 'this scene is the climax, amplify everything' vs 'this scene is transition, keep it subtle.'
examples: { level: 'scene', id: 'scene-7', weight: 0.85, parent: 'product-demo' }

nodes.name: Moment-level Weights (under 3 minute content)
nodes.summary: For short content or critical moments in any length. LLM marks specific sentences/timestamps with fine-grained reasoning.

details.definition: Short content (under 3 minutes): Moment-level weights. The LLM can mark specific sentences or timestamps. 'The claim at 0:47 is weight 0.9.' Fine-grained enough for the LLM to reason about every significant moment.
examples: { level: 'moment', timestamp_ms: 47000, weight: 1.0, parent: 'scene-7' }

nodes.name: Weight Resolution Rules
nodes.summary: Resolution chain: moment-level weight > parent scene weight > parent section weight > 0.5 default.

details.definition: If a moment-level weight exists for the current timestamp, use it. Otherwise, use the parent scene-level weight. Otherwise, use the parent section-level weight. If no weight data at all, use 0.5 (neutral, no modification).
examples: moment > scene > section > 0.5

nodes.name: Cold-Start Fallback Values
nodes.summary: Conservative middle-ground defaults used ONLY when signal computation fails (e.g., text brief only, no footage or script). Thompson Sampling moves away quickly.

details.definition: In rare cases where no signals are available yet (e.g., user provides only a text brief with no footage or script), these FALLBACK values are used. They are intentionally conservative middle-ground values. Thompson Sampling will move away from these quickly.
details.fallback: pacing=5, energy=0.45, transitions=10, graphics=3, silence=1.0, zooms=5, formality=0.5
details.rationale: These are NOT content-type presets. There is deliberately ONE fallback, not eight. The system should compute from signals whenever possible.

nodes.name: HIGH Confidence
nodes.summary: Computed from 5+ minutes of clean footage with speech + visual analysis. Most reliable training signal for Thompson Sampling.

details.definition: HIGH confidence: Computed from 5+ minutes of clean footage with speech + visual analysis
details.rationale: Thompson Sampling weighs its learning rate by confidence — high-confidence computations are more reliable training signals than low-confidence guesses.

nodes.name: MEDIUM Confidence
nodes.summary: Computed from transcript only (Mode 1 with script, no footage yet).

details.definition: MEDIUM confidence: Computed from transcript only (Mode 1 with script, no footage yet)

nodes.name: LOW Confidence
nodes.summary: Computed from brief/title only, or cold-start fallback. Least reliable training signal.

details.definition: LOW confidence: Computed from brief/title only, or cold-start fallback

nodes.name: Universal Override Principle
nodes.summary: Every decision the system makes is manually overridable. The automatic car model: auto mode drives, but the human can grab the wheel without crashing. Every override logged to Graphiti.

details.definition: Every decision the system makes is manually overridable. Changing one decision does not break others. The automatic car model: auto mode drives, but the human can grab the wheel at any point without crashing.
details.rationale: Every override gets logged to Graphiti as a learning signal for Thompson Sampling. 'User overrode zoom_punch to zoom_push for this brand' → system adjusts future behavior.
examples: Genre parameters? User can adjust any dial manually
Moment weights? User can reweight any moment/scene/section
Signal→technique mappings? User can disable specific techniques ('no stat graphics in this video')
Compositional constraints? User can override ('I know these color temps clash, I want the dissolve anyway')
Technical constants? User can override LUFS target, safe zones, caption timing for specific creative reasons
Any individual edit decision? User can change one zoom without re-running the pipeline

nodes.name: Priority 1: User's Project Brief / Brand Guidelines
nodes.summary: If user provided specific text to display, use it. Highest priority for on-screen text.

details.definition: Priority 1: User's project brief / brand guidelines (if they provided specific text to display)

nodes.name: Priority 2: Cleaned Transcript
nodes.summary: Same fact, professional phrasing. Number/fact must come from transcript; phrasing can be cleaned. No added claims.

details.definition: Priority 2: Cleaned transcript — same fact, professional phrasing. Rule: The NUMBER/FACT must come from the transcript. The PHRASING can be cleaned up. Allowed: Remove fillers, abbreviate, format numbers, add units. Not allowed: Add claims ('Industry Leading'), change the number, editorialize
examples: Speaker says 'um we actually grew like three hundred percent year over year'
Graphic shows: '300% YoY Growth'

nodes.name: Priority 3: Exact Transcript (verbatim)
nodes.summary: Verbatim what was said — safest fallback when cleaning is risky.

details.definition: Priority 3: Exact transcript — verbatim what was said (safest fallback)

nodes.name: NEVER: AI-generated Claims
nodes.summary: NEVER add superlatives, characterizations, or claims not in source material. If the speaker didn't say it, it doesn't go on screen.

details.definition: NEVER: AI-generated claims, superlatives, or characterizations not in the source material. If the speaker didn't say it, it doesn't go on screen.
